name: Issue Management Plan
one_liner: How unplanned events that have already happened get logged, owned and resolved.
purpose: Defines and documents the activities, roles and responsibilities related to identifying, assessing, assigning, resolving and controlling project issues — unplanned project-related events that require a project management action. The process helps the Project Manager act on anything with a potential impact on scope, time, cost, quality, risk or stakeholder satisfaction. An Issue Log records identification, evaluation, assignment and deadlines, while related decisions are recorded in a Decision Log.

fields.what: States that the plan defines the activities, roles and responsibilities for identifying, assessing, assigning, resolving and controlling project issues, and for documenting decisions and their owners.
fields.castor: Issue and decision management for Project CASTOR, LOS renewal, 26 months.

fields.what: An unplanned, project-related event that has already happened and requires a project management action: the intervention of the PM or higher management. Anyone can raise one.
fields.castor: Anything already blocking CASTOR delivery that the PCT cannot clear itself.

fields.what: Ensure that issues with a potential impact on project scope, time, cost, quality, risk or stakeholder satisfaction are assessed and acted upon, and logged in the Issue Log.
fields.castor: No issue of impact 3 or above may sit unassigned beyond one status meeting.

fields.what: Key decisions are logged in a Decision Log, which brings visibility to decisions and accountability for how and by whom they were taken and to whom they must be communicated.
fields.castor: DEC-011 and DEC-012 both taken at the PSC of 12 Oct 2027.

fields.what: Any stakeholder can raise an issue through any channel. The PM registers it in the Issue Log; PCT members may register issues directly, subject to PM validation.
fields.castor: Gustave Eiffel notified the architect's resignation by email on 04 Oct 2027.

fields.what: Disagreements on the interpretation of requirements; PCT unable to meet time, resource or quality goals; non-conformities found by the team or quality assurance; risks that occur; adverse external effects.
fields.who: PM screens · BM flags business issues
fields.castor: Non-conformities raised by W. Edwards Deming (PQA) go straight into the Issue Log.

fields.f: Step 2: Issue Assessment and Action Recommendation
fields.what: Assess urgency and impact and set a resolution priority. The raiser makes an informal first assessment of category, impact, urgency and size; urgent issues reach the PM immediately.
fields.castor: ISS-012 flagged urgent by Gustave Eiffel; PM informed the same day.

fields.what: The PM assigns detailed analysis to a stakeholder, who identifies the root cause, recommends a solution and details steps, effort and resources, all documented in the Issue Log.
fields.castor: Root cause of ISS-012: single point of design knowledge at the contractor.

fields.what: Ishikawa: describe the symptoms, categorise potential causes, probe the explanations behind each to reach the root cause, then plan actions. Pareto: rank issue categories by frequency, tackle the most frequent.
fields.castor: Fishbone on data-migration breaks; Pareto showed 62% of parallel-run defects were configuration.

fields.what: Once issues are evaluated and remediation actions approved, the PM incorporates them into the Project Work Plan and updates related plans and logs: Decision Log, Resource Plan, Change Log.
fields.castor: ISS-012 handover became Work Plan tasks 6.2 and 6.3, three weeks of effort.

fields.what: Monitor and control identified issues so they can be communicated to each decision layer for action approval or status update; the PM keeps the Issue Log current.
fields.castor: Issue Log reviewed every Tuesday at the weekly Project Status Meeting.

fields.what: PSC consulted on remediation actions and informed monthly; PO accountable and approves major actions; BM and SP consulted on assessment; PM responsible; PCT consulted and resolves; BIG can raise issues.
fields.castor: Leonardo da Vinci consulted on ISS-012; Grace Hopper owns business-side issues.

fields.what: Two rows: the Issue Management Plan (I, I, A, C, C, I, R, C) and the Manage Issues & Decisions process (I, I, A, S, C, I, R, C).
fields.castor: BM shifts from Consulted on the plan to Supports when issues are managed.

fields.what: Techniques used to analyse issues — Ishikawa diagram, Pareto diagram, root cause analysis — and the tools used to manage them: the Issue Log and the Decision Log.
fields.castor: PM² Issue Log and Decision Log used unchanged, held in the PSO project folder.

fields.what: Identification block (ID, category, title, description, status, identified by, date) plus assessment block (action details, urgency, impact, size, target date, issue owner, escalation, traceability).
fields.castor: Issue categories mirror the risk categories, so risk-to-issue transfers keep their label.

fields.what: Open (identified, needs attention and if possible a resolution), Postponed (resolution deferred for other priorities), Resolved (all actions completed), Closed (all work completed and verified).
fields.castor: ISS-012 Open 05 Oct 2027, Resolved 02 Nov 2027, Closed 09 Nov 2027.

fields.what: Three separate 1–5 scales (5=Very high): Urgency is how fast a solution is needed, Impact the consequence of the issue, Size the effort to resolve it.
fields.castor: ISS-012 scored Urgency 4, Impact 4, Size 3.

fields.what: Identification (ID, category, title, description, identified by, people present, comments), ownership (decision owner, decision date, escalation) and implementation (date of application, communicated to).
fields.castor: DEC-012 records who attended the PSC and who must be told the outcome.

fields.what: Describes how issues are detected and recorded. Only issues that cannot be solved easily and that require a management action should be registered in the Issue Log.
fields.castor: Day-to-day defects stay in the test tracker; only escalated ones become issues.

fields.what: Any project activity — for example small meeting actions — that does not appear in the Project Work Plan should be logged, assigned and tracked using the Issue Log.
fields.castor: Actions from the weekly status meeting tracked in the Issue Log, not in a side list.

fields.f: Risk that materialises becomes an issue
fields.what: Any risk that materialises and requires action creates an issue, logged, assessed, assigned and tracked in the Issue Log; the risk itself is closed in the Risk Log.
fields.castor: R-07 occurred on 04 Oct 2027 and became ISS-012; R-07 closed 26 Oct 2027.

fields.f: Issues that lead to project change
fields.what: Issues of significant size may lead to a project change; those issues follow the project change management process and are also tracked through the Change Log.
fields.castor: ISS-012 replanning stayed inside baseline, so no Change Request was needed.

fields.what: Very Low and Low size/impact remediation actions are approved at the Managing Layer (BM and PM); all others by the PSC; major issues reported yearly to the AGB.
fields.who: PM applies · PO owns the rule
fields.castor: ISS-012 escalated: impact 4 exceeded the Managing Layer's authority; AGB told yearly.

fields.what: Issues are tracked together with key decisions. Decisions at Managing, Directing or Steering Layer are documented in the Decision Log, cross-referring to related issues, risks or changes.
fields.castor: DEC-012 refers back to ISS-012 and to closed risk R-07.

fields.what: States where remediation actions and their status are recorded and monitored — principally the Project Work Plan, plus any other tracking documents or tools used by the project.
fields.castor: All remediation actions above two person-days become Work Plan tasks.

fields.what: New or open issues are followed up weekly at Project Status Meetings and assigned to a responsible party; the PM then updates the Issue Log with the review results.
fields.castor: Weekly Tuesday status meeting; monthly issue summary in the PSC pack.

fields.what: An issue cannot be eliminated without an assessment that it is no longer occurring; the PM must verify closure and may re-open the issue if it recurs.
fields.castor: ISS-018 (reconciliation acceptance) re-opened once before partial acceptance held.

fields.what: When an issue is closed and validated by the PM, the person responsible for the resolution updates the project's Lessons Learned in the Issue Log.
fields.castor: Lesson from ISS-012: require named deputies for every contractor key role.

fields.what: Cross-references the Project Handbook (escalation and conflict resolution), the Communications Management Plan (reporting) and the Risk Management Plan (risks that may become issues).
fields.castor: Handbook, Communications and Risk plans, all version 1.0 of 26 Jun 2026.

fields.what: Lists related documents by title, version, date and location: Handbook, Risk Management Plan, Communications Management Plan, Issue Log, Decision Log and the project folder.
fields.castor: 24.Issue_Log.CASTOR.xlsx and 25.Decision_Log.CASTOR.xlsx in the PSO folder.

traps: Issue = already happened. Risk = uncertain future event. Change = altering a baseline.
The plan defines the process; the Issue Log and Decision Log hold the instances.
Issue Log scores Urgency, Impact and Size — never likelihood; that belongs to risk.
Only issues needing a management action are logged, not every problem.
Issue and Decision Logs are set up in Initiating; this plan only defines their structure.
